twoFlavours.remarks: This operation has two overloads: one taking BuildPipeline, and one taking InputSpec<BuildPipeline> for use after a stage that declares CLI inputs. Both apply the same setting to the pipeline.

pipelineDefault.remarks: Settings declared on a pipeline act as defaults for all stages unless overridden at the stage level. A stage-level setting takes precedence over the pipeline's.

timeoutUnits.remarks: Accepts int<second>, float seconds, or a TimeSpan. All are converted internally to TimeSpan.

acceptableExitCodes.remarks: By default, only exit code 0 is acceptable. Setting this replaces (rather than appends to) the acceptable codes. A stage-level setting overrides the pipeline's.

envVars.remarks: Appends to the pipeline's environment variables rather than replacing them. Keys set here override any inherited from parent contexts. A stage can declare additional variables that shadow these.

postStages.remarks: Post stages run after the main stages whether or not the pipeline succeeded, which makes them the place for teardown. Setting this replaces any post stages already declared rather than appending.

hooks.remarks: Setting this replaces the previous hook rather than chaining onto it. The hook receives the StageContext of the stage it brackets, and runs for every stage in the pipeline.

mirror.remarks: This is the InputSpec<BuildPipeline> mirror of the operation of the same name. It exists so that a setting placed after a stage that declares CLI inputs is still accepted; without it the placement would be an overload error rather than a no-op. The behaviour is identical.
